_metadata.rubric: x04 rubric (natural-click standard + five content questions), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the single input file x04b-rb-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: Classic picnic scene: ants invade picnics (ANT) and picnics happen in the park (PARK); instant and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean scene clue.

hints.reason: Icebergs calve off Antarctica (ANTARCTICA) and are the famous hazard to ships, Titanic-style (SHIP); both sides are immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; slightly less vivid than the TITANIC version of the same idea.

hints.reason: Icebergs break off Antarctica (ANTARCTICA) and an iceberg sank the Titanic (TITANIC); the Titanic side is about as instant as a clue gets.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, easy click.

hints.reason: Apollo astronauts (ASTRONAUT) plus Apollo the Greek sun/light god (SUN); the mythology side takes a beat but is widely known, and the double meaning is satisfying.
hints.fix: Apollo is the Greek god of light, often linked with the sun.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning. Strictly, Helios is the Greek sun god and Apollo was later identified with him; the softer line avoids overstating it.

hints.reason: Apollo program astronauts (ASTRONAUT) and Harlem's Apollo Theater (THEATER); the theater is a well-known American landmark, so the second side clicks after a moment.

pairs.pair_note: Anchored by the strong astronaut side; Apollo Theater is moderately but broadly known in the U.S.

hints.reason: Picnic basket (BASKET) and Yogi Bear's "pic-a-nic basket" thefts (BEAR); the pair itself is Yogi's catchphrase, a real oh-nice moment.

pairs.pair_note: Best of the PICNIC pairs: BASKET + BEAR is the Yogi Bear image in full.

hints.reason: "Pitch black" (BLACK) is an instant phrase and a voice's pitch (VOICE) is everyday vocabulary; two different senses of PITCH, both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase join on one side, but both halves are immediate and the sense shift is pleasant.

hints.reason: Picnic blanket (BLANKET) spread out in the park (PARK); a clear, easy scene.

hints.reason: Apollo Creed, Rocky's rival champion (BOXER), and NASA's Apollo Moon program (NASA); both meanings are famous and the pop-culture swerve is fun.

hints.reason: A business pitch to investors, Shark Tank-style (BUSINESS), and the compound pitchfork (FORK); both are instantly familiar.

hints.reason: A sales or investor pitch (BUSINESS) and vocal pitch (VOICE); two everyday senses of the word.

pairs.pair_note: Solid double meaning.

hints.reason: A referee's striped shirt (REFEREE) is instant; CANE needs the step to candy cane stripes, which comes quickly.

pairs.pair_note: CANE is the weaker side across all STRIPES pairs because the board shows CANE, not CANDY CANE; still a fair visual link.

hints.reason: CANE needs the candy-cane step and STAR comes only through the phrase "Stars and Stripes" (stars themselves are not striped), so both sides are second-step; CHRISTMAS (candy canes on the tree, a star on top) is a clearly stronger single scene.

pairs.pair_note: Text is accurate, but CHRISTMAS (or TREE) unifies this pair far better than STRIPES.

hints.reason: Tiger stripes (TIGER) are instant and candy cane stripes (CANE) follow with a moment's thought; a fair visual link.

pairs.pair_note: Easy shared-property clue; cane side slightly softer.

hints.reason: Zebra stripes (ZEBRA) are the defining image and candy cane stripes (CANE) come quickly; simple but fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; the striped-candy image is a pleasant contrast with the zebra.

hints.reason: Pitchfork (FORK) as a compound and vocal pitch (VOICE); both instantly familiar, with a bonus that a tuning fork sets pitch.

pairs.pair_note: Tuning fork gives a second, musical route to FORK; the explanation could mention it, but the current text is accurate.

hints.reason: The two targets together make "ghost story", the classic campfire tale (GHOST and STORY), much like PAPER + CRANE -> ORIGAMI; instant and satisfying.
hints.fix: Telling ghost stories is a classic campfire tradition.

pairs.pair_note: Strong idea, but the explanation repeats the same fact twice; a single sentence (the fix) reads better, and the two lines could become "Spooky tales of ghosts..." and "...are classic campfire stories."

hints.reason: Camping scene: a tent by the campfire (TENT) and ghost stories told around it (GHOST); the ghost side goes through "ghost stories" but lands quickly.
